posts.title: 39 Gold Metallic Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Gold metallic nails, all 39 of them: true mirror gold, champagne chrome, rose gold shine, gold French tips and foil-gold glam, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Gold is the warm metal, and in chrome form it reads like jewelry you never take off. These **39 gold metallic nail ideas** collect the whole range: true mirror gold, soft champagne chrome, rose gold shine, gold French tips and foil-gold party sets, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 gold metallic designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your gold before you book. Yellow mirror gold is the boldest and reads richest on warm skin; champagne gold is the soft everyday version; rose gold chrome sits in between and flatters everyone. Gold French tips keep the metal only at the edge for the office-safe take. Shapes follow the metal: almond and oval show the mirror unbroken, coffin carries the full glam brief. The full collection lives in the Gold Metallic topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: metallic chrome lives or dies on the base. Ask for a smooth, fully cured gel base, chrome powder rubbed in and sealed with a hard gel top coat, free edge sealed at every layer, so the gold does not rub off at the tips. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What shades of gold chrome are there?
faq.a: Yellow mirror gold is the richest, champagne gold the softest, and rose gold chrome the in-between flatterer: design 1 (Gold Mirror Stiletto on Dark Skin) shows the full mirror, while design 11 (Gold Glitter Coffin Duo) shows the softer everyday take.

faq.q: Do gold metallic nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. Gold chrome wraps short shapes beautifully and reads like jewelry at any length. Design 4 (Gold Mirror Almond Clasped) and design 21 (Gold Swirl Almond Duo on Dark Skin Bright) prove the shine keeps its impact short.

faq.q: What gold nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Warm mirror gold is a standout on dark and brown skin: the metal glows against deeper skin and never reads dull. See design 2 (Champagne Gold Almond in Knit), design 16 (Gold Mirror Square Close-Up) and design 31 (Gold French Short Duo with Rings).

faq.q: How do I keep gold chrome from rubbing off at the tips?
faq.a: Sealing is everything. Ask for chrome sealed under a hard gel top coat with the free edge sealed at every layer, like design 26 (Gold Glitter Almond Duo Palms), and re-oil cuticles daily.

faq.q: Can gold metallic nails be worn every day?
faq.a: Yes, in the champagne and French versions. A soft gold like design 16 (Gold Mirror Square Close-Up) reads polished at work; save the full mirror for the statement days.

intro: Emerald is the jewel of the green family: deeper than sage, richer than forest, and it flatters every skin tone it touches. These **36 emerald green nail ideas** collect the whole range: true emerald gloss, deep green chrome, velvet and cat eye finishes, emerald-and-gold glam, marble greens and green French tips, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 emerald green designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your emerald before you book. The glossy jewel version is the everyday signature: polished, rich, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Velvet and cat eye greens are the light-catching party picks, chrome green is the metal statement, and emerald with gold accents is the holiday-season glam. Shapes follow the color: almond and oval keep it elegant, coffin and stiletto carry the drama, short square emerald is the practical rich pick. The full collection lives in the Emerald Green topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: deep green pigment needs thin, fully cured layers or it wrinkles and fades at the edges. Ask for gel built in thin coats, a hard gel top coat, and the free edge sealed at every layer so the jewel tone stays deep. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What shades count as emerald green nails?
faq.a: True emerald is the deep jewel green; the family runs from bright jewel gloss to near-black deep green. Design 1 (Emerald Almond) shows the classic jewel, while design 11 (Emerald Almond with Gold Glitter Accent) shows the deeper evening version.

faq.q: Do emerald green nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. Deep green concentrates beautifully at short length and short square emerald is a signature rich look. Design 4 (Emerald Cat Eye Oval Duo) and design 21 (Emerald Chrome Almond with Gold Rings) prove the color keeps its depth short.

faq.q: What emerald green nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Emerald is one of the great colors on dark and brown skin: the jewel tone reads rich and luminous, never muddy, especially with gold accents. See design 2 (Dark Emerald Oval with Orchid), design 16 (Emerald Short Square Duo) and design 31 (Emerald Coffin with Glitter Accent in Towel).

faq.q: How do I keep dark green nails from fading or wrinkling?
faq.a: Thin layers, fully cured, sealed under a hard gel top coat with the free edge sealed at every layer, like design 26 (Emerald Gold Foil Square Close-Up); deep pigments punish thick coats.

faq.q: Are emerald nails only for winter?
faq.a: They peak in the holiday season but wear all year: a clean emerald like design 16 (Emerald Short Square Duo) is an everyday signature, and the velvet versions carry the party months.

posts.title: 39 Snowflake Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Snowflake nails, all 39 of them: hand-painted flakes on icy blue, white and deep winter bases, silver glitter frost, pearl and chrome snow finishes and snowflake French tips, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Snowflakes are the signature art of the winter set: fine white linework, icy bases and frost that catches the light. These **39 snowflake nail ideas** collect the whole range: classic white flakes on icy blue and deep winter bases, silver glitter frost, pearl and chrome snow finishes, and snowflake French tips, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 snowflake designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your flake before you book. The hand-painted version on a deep base is the statement: high contrast, unmistakably winter. Glitter frost is the party pick, pearl and milky white are the soft everyday versions, and a snowflake accent nail over a clean French is the minimal route. Shapes follow the art: almond and coffin give the flakes canvas, short square keeps it practical. The full collection lives in the Snowflake topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: snowflake linework is only as good as its cure. Ask for thin white gel lines, flash-cured flake by flake so nothing bleeds, and everything sealed under a hard top coat. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What base colors work best under snowflake nails?
faq.a: Any base with contrast: icy blue, navy, burgundy and deep green make white flakes pop, while milky white and pearl give the soft tone-on-tone look. Design 1 (Snowflake Ombre Coffin Duo) shows the classic contrast version, while design 11 (Blue French Snowflake Duo) shows the softer route.

faq.q: Do snowflake nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. One small flake per nail reads perfectly at short length, and short square snowflakes are a signature winter look. Design 4 (Grey Knit Snowflake Oval) and design 21 (French Snowflake Square with Rings) prove the art keeps its detail short.

faq.q: What snowflake nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Snowflakes are brilliant on dark and brown skin: white linework and icy bases read bright and crisp, never washed out, especially over deep blue or burgundy. See design 2 (Royal Blue Snowflake Oval Duo), design 16 (Glitter Tip Snowflake Short) and design 31 (Pearl Chrome Snowflakes in Knit).

faq.q: How do I keep fine snowflake linework from chipping?
faq.a: Thin gel lines, flash-cured as they are painted, then sealed under a hard top coat, like design 26 (Milky Snowflake Short); thick uncured lines are what lift and blur.

faq.q: Are snowflake nails only for Christmas week?
faq.a: They peak in December but wear all winter: a clean snowflake like design 16 (Glitter Tip Snowflake Short) is a January signature too, long after the tree comes down.

posts.title: 38 Velvet Red Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Velvet red nails, all 38 of them: magnetic cat-eye velvet, deep wine and burgundy velvets, black-red ombres, matte flock velvet, red velvet French tips and glitter velvets, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Velvet is the finish that made red magnetic: a cat-eye stripe that rolls across the nail like light on fabric. These **38 velvet red nail ideas** collect the whole range: true velvet cat eye, deep wine and burgundy velvets, black-red ombres, true matte flock velvet, red velvet French tips and glitter velvets, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 velvet red designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your velvet before you book. The centered-stripe gloss version is the everyday signature: rich, dimensional, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Black-red ombre velvet is the dramatic evening pick, matte flock is the true fabric look, and a red velvet French tip is the minimal route. Shapes follow the finish: almond and coffin give the stripe room to roll, short square velvet is the practical rich pick. The full collection lives in the Velvet Red topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: velvet is a magnet technique, not a polish. Ask for magnetic gel, the magnet held close for a few seconds on every nail before curing, and a second magnet pass over the top coat if you want the stripe at full strength. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What exactly are velvet nails?
faq.a: Velvet nails use magnetic gel polish: a magnet pulls the particles into a soft band of light that shifts as the nail moves, like velvet fabric. Design 1 (Velvet Red Stiletto Duo) shows the classic centered stripe, while design 11 (Red Chrome Coffin Close-Up) shows the darker ombre version.

faq.q: Do velvet red nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. The stripe concentrates beautifully at short length and short square velvet red is a signature rich look. Design 4 (Red Black Ombre Coffin) and design 21 (Velvet Red Almond Duo on Fur) prove the effect keeps its depth short.

faq.q: What velvet red nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Velvet red is luminous on dark and brown skin: the magnetic band reads like lit fabric and deep wine shades never go muddy. See design 2 (Velvet Red Cat Eye Almond), design 16 (Velvet Foil Almond in Knit) and design 31 (Red Black Ombre Stiletto Duo).

faq.q: How do I keep the velvet stripe strong?
faq.a: The magnet pass is everything: held close a few seconds per nail before curing, and repeated over the top coat, like design 26 (Red Glitter Velvet Cherry Accent); a rushed magnet pass is what makes velvet look flat.

faq.q: Are velvet red nails only for the holidays?
faq.a: They peak in party season but wear all year: a clean velvet red like design 16 (Velvet Foil Almond in Knit) is an everyday signature, and the black-red versions carry the evening months.

posts.title: 36 Winter Almond Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Winter almond nails, all 36 of them: milky whites and snow-day nudes, cocoa and burgundy almonds, navy and forest winter shades, plaid and sweater textures, chrome and glitter finishes and winter French tips, on real hands and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Almond is the shape winter was made for: elegant like a stiletto, practical like an oval, and long enough to carry every cold-weather shade. These **36 winter almond nail ideas** collect the whole season: milky whites and snow-day nudes, cocoa and burgundy almonds, navy and forest winter shades, plaid and sweater textures, chrome and glitter finishes and winter French tips. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 winter almond designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your winter lane before you book. Milky white and nude almonds are the everyday signatures: soft, brightening, and they hide regrowth for weeks. Cocoa, burgundy and navy are the rich winter picks, plaid and sweater textures are the cozy statement, and chrome is the party finish. Length follows lifestyle: medium almond is the sweet spot that survives gloves and typing. The full collection lives in the Winter Almond topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: winter is hard on nails, so the shape matters. Almond distributes stress better than square corners, which is why these sets survive the dry season; ask for gel or gel extensions, cuticle oil daily, and bring the photo of your pick: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: Why is almond the best winter shape?
faq.a: Almond has no sharp corners to catch on gloves, coats and knits, and the tapered sides distribute stress, so sets survive the dry season better. Design 1 (Burgundy Snowflake Almond on Fur) shows the classic medium almond most of this list is built on.

faq.q: What winter colors suit almond nails best?
faq.a: Milky whites and nudes for everyday, cocoa and burgundy for richness, navy and forest for drama. See design 4 (Chocolate Almond with Gold Ring) for the soft end and design 21 (Emerald Silver Almond Duo) for the deep shades.

faq.q: Do winter almond nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Beautifully: winter shades glow on dark and brown skin and milky tones brighten against it. See design 2 (Emerald Leaf Art Almond), design 16 (Plaid Mix Short Almond Duo) and design 31 (Blue French Almond Duo in Snow).

faq.q: What length should winter almonds be?
faq.a: Medium is the sweet spot: long enough for the elegant taper, short enough for gloves and typing, like design 26 (Nude French Snowflake Almond); go longer only for party weeks.

faq.q: How do I stop winter nails breaking?
faq.a: The almond shape itself helps; add gel or gel extensions for strength, cuticle oil daily against dry air, and a shape like design 11 (White Line Art Almond on Dark Skin) with no square corners to snag.

posts.title: 37 Icy Blue Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Icy blue nails, all 37 of them: pale ice and baby blue, frosty chrome and glazed finishes, icy French tips, glitter frost, snow-day marble and cat eye ice, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Icy blue is the frozen end of the winter palette: pale, glassy and cold in the best way. These **37 icy blue nail ideas** collect the whole range: pale ice and baby blue, frosty chrome and glazed finishes, icy French tips, glitter frost, snow-day marble and cat eye ice, with deep frozen navy for contrast. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 icy blue designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your ice level before you book. Pale milky blue is the everyday signature: clean, brightening, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Frosty chrome and glazed ice are the statement finishes, an icy French tip is the minimal route, and glitter frost is the party pick. Shapes follow the finish: almond and oval keep it soft, square makes it crisp. The full collection lives in the Icy Blue topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: icy blue is unforgiving about shade. Too warm and it reads baby shower, too grey and it goes dull; the sweet spot is a cool, slightly translucent blue, ideally over a milky base. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as icy blue?
faq.a: A cool, pale blue with a frozen, glassy feel: think ice, frost and glacier water rather than sky. Design 1 (Icy Blue Coffin Crystal Accent) is the reference shade, while design 11 (Baby Blue Stiletto Snowflakes) shows the chrome version.

faq.q: Do icy blue nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, and they pop: the pale cool blue contrasts beautifully with dark and brown skin and the chrome versions glow. See design 2 (Grey Blue Snowflake Almond), design 16 (Blue Ombre Chrome Almond) and design 31 (Silver Chrome Almond at Pinecones).

faq.q: Icy blue or baby blue: what is the difference?
faq.a: Baby blue is warmer and creamier; icy blue is cooler, paler and usually translucent or glazed. Design 4 (Baby Blue Ombre Coffin on Dark Skin) sits on the icy side, while the softest sets here lean baby.

faq.q: What finish makes blue look frozen?
faq.a: Chrome rubs, glazed (milky glass) top coats and fine glitter frost. Design 21 (Blue Snowflake Chrome Duo) shows the glazed route; ask for the same finish at any length.

faq.q: Are icy blue nails only for winter?
faq.a: They peak in winter but the pale chrome versions wear as a cool neutral all year; a clean icy set like design 26 (Periwinkle Glitter Snowflake Duo) is seasonless.

posts.excerpt: Pearl white nails, all 38 of them: glazed pearl chrome and iridescent shine, milky pearl whites, bridal-clean French tips and pearl accent nails, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Pearl white is the luminous end of the white palette: glazed, glowing and clean in the best way. These **38 pearl white nail ideas** collect the whole range: glazed pearl chrome and iridescent shine, milky pearl whites, bridal-clean French tips and pearl accent nails, with soft shimmer finishes throughout. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 pearl white designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your glow level before you book. Milky pearl is the everyday signature: clean, brightening, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Glazed chrome pearl is the statement finish, a pearl French tip is the minimal route, and a single pearl accent nail is the subtle pick. Shapes follow the finish: almond and oval keep it soft, square makes it crisp. The full collection lives in the Pearl White topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: pearl white is unforgiving about base color. Too stark and it reads chalky, too sheer and it disappears; the sweet spot is a milky white under a pearl chrome rub. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as pearl white?
faq.a: A luminous white with a pearlescent glow: think glazed, iridescent and softly shiny rather than flat white. Design 1 (Full Pearl Coffin on Dark Skin) is the reference finish, while design 11 (Pearl Chrome Short Duo in Knit) shows the chrome version.

faq.q: Do pearl white nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, beautifully: the luminous white contrasts and glows on dark and brown skin. See design 2 (Pearl Cluster Square on Cotton), design 16 (Pearl Cluster Coffin in Palm on Dark Skin) and design 31 (Pearl Chrome Short Duo on Silk).

faq.q: Pearl white or milky white: what is the difference?
faq.a: Milky white is a soft translucent white with no shimmer; pearl white adds the pearlescent chrome glow on top. Design 4 (Glossy Pearl Almond Duo) sits on the pearl side, while the softest sets here lean milky.

faq.q: What finish makes white look luminous?
faq.a: Pearl chrome rubs, glazed top coats and fine iridescent shimmer. Design 21 (Opal Pearl Oval in Palm) shows the glazed route; ask for the same finish at any length.

faq.q: Are pearl white nails only for weddings?
faq.a: They peak at weddings but the clean pearl versions wear as a polished neutral all year; a set like design 26 (Blue Pearl Oval Duo with Ring) is seasonless.

faq.a: A mirror-metallic finish in a warm pink-gold tone, usually chrome powder rubbed over a blush or nude gel base. Design 1 (Mirror Rose Gold Stiletto Duo on Dark Skin) is the reference shine, while design 11 (Blush Jelly Almond with Chrome Edge) shows the softer metallic version.

faq.q: Do rose gold chrome nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, they glow: the warm metal flatters dark and brown skin especially. See design 2 (Mirror Rose Gold Oval Macro), design 16 (Gold Glitter Chrome Coffin Duo) and design 31 (Rose Chrome Stiletto Duo Duo).

faq.q: Rose gold chrome or pink chrome: what is the difference?
faq.a: Pink chrome is cooler and more candy-toned; rose gold is warmer, with the gold pulling it toward jewelry metal. Design 4 (Black Art Almond with Rose Glitter) sits on the rose gold side.

faq.q: How long does chrome last?
faq.a: With a structured gel base and a no-wipe top coat, chrome wears like regular gel: two to three weeks. Design 21 (Silver Tip Ombre Stiletto Duo) shows the full-mirror version worth protecting.

faq.q: Can rose gold chrome be subtle?
faq.a: Yes: a French tip or a single chrome accent nail keeps it office-friendly. Design 26 (Blush Chrome Short Duo) is the restrained route.

posts.title: 36 Short Winter Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Short winter nails, all 36 of them: snowflake art and frosty whites, short burgundy and deep red, cozy glitter, short French tips and winter neutrals at practical lengths, on square, oval, almond and round shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Short winter is the practical end of the cold-season palette: every winter design, at a length you can type, cook and live in. These **36 short winter nail ideas** collect the whole range: snowflake art and frosty whites, short burgundy and deep red, cozy glitter and short French tips, navy and winter neutrals. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 180 short winter designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your winter mood before you book. Frosty white and snowflake art are the December signature, burgundy is the everyday classic, glitter is the party pick, and a short French tip is the minimal route. Shapes follow the hand: oval and almond soften short nails, square makes them crisp. The full collection lives in the Short Winter topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: short nails are a design constraint, not a compromise. Art has to be scaled, fine lines have to be finer, and dark colors need a clean edge to look expensive. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as a short winter nail?
faq.a: A practical, near-fingertip length in a cold-season palette or design: frosty whites, snowflakes, burgundy, navy, cozy glitter. Design 1 (Nude Short with Snowflake Accent in Cream Knit) is the reference set, while design 11 (Christmas Mix Short Duo) shows the art-led version.

faq.q: Do short winter nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes: deep winter colors and bright frosty whites both pop on dark and brown skin. See design 2 (Christmas Art Short Duo), design 16 (Blush Short Duo with Snowflake Accent in Purple Knit) and design 31 (Olive Short Duo with Tree Accent at Garland).

faq.q: Can you do nail art on short nails?
faq.a: Absolutely, it just has to be scaled: finer snowflakes, tip-concentrated designs, single-accent nails. Design 4 (Forest Green Short with Snowflake Accent) shows the scaled route done right.

faq.q: What shape is best for short winter nails?
faq.a: Oval and almond soften and lengthen the look of short nails; square is crisper and more modern. Design 21 (Snowflake Glitter Tip Short Duo in Knit) shows the soft route.

faq.q: How do short sets hold up in winter?
faq.a: Better than long ones: less leverage, fewer breaks, and gloves go on without a fight. A gel set like design 26 (Black Snowflake Short Duo Duo) easily lasts two to three weeks.

posts.title: 39 Plum Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Plum nails, all 39 of them: rich plum and dark eggplant, plum chrome and cat eye depth, plum glitter and marble, matte plum and French tips, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Plum is the deep end of the purple palette: rich, wine-dark and dramatic in the best way. These **39 plum nail ideas** collect the whole range: rich plum and dark eggplant, plum chrome and cat eye depth, plum glitter and marble, matte plum and plum French tips. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 198 plum designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your depth before you book. Glossy rich plum is the everyday signature: saturated, polished, seasonless-dark. Cat eye and chrome are the statement finishes, matte plum is the moody route, and a plum French tip is the minimal pick. Shapes follow the color: almond and coffin keep it elegant, square makes it sharp. The full collection lives in the Plum topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: plum is unforgiving about coats. Too thin and it goes patchy, too thick and it floods; the sweet spot is two thin, fully cured coats over a smooth base. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as plum?
faq.a: A deep, wine-rich purple: darker and warmer than lavender or violet, lighter than near-black eggplant at its deepest. Design 1 (Deep Plum Matte with Chrome Gem Accents) is the reference shade, while design 11 (Burgundy Stiletto Duo on Fur) shows the chrome version.

faq.q: Do plum nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, they are made for each other: the rich purple glows on dark and brown skin. See design 2 (Plum Glitter Stiletto Duo), design 16 (Glossy Plum Almond Duo) and design 31 (Plum Cat Eye Almond Duo Duo).

faq.q: Plum or burgundy: what is the difference?
faq.a: Burgundy leans red-wine; plum leans purple-wine. Design 4 (Matte Violet Almond Duo Outdoors) sits firmly on the plum side, while the warmest sets here borrow a little burgundy light.

faq.q: What finish suits plum best?
faq.a: High gloss for richness, cat eye for dimension, matte for mood. Design 21 (Violet Coffin Duo with Gold Art) shows the dimensional route; ask for the same finish at any length.

faq.q: Are plum nails only for fall and winter?
faq.a: They peak in the cold months but a clean glossy plum wears as a rich neutral-dark all year; a set like design 26 (Plum Almond Duo in Cream Knit) is seasonless.

posts.title: 40 New Year's Eve Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: New Year's Eve nails, all 40 of them: champagne gold and silver glitter, black-and-gold drama, midnight blue sparkle, confetti art and chrome party shine, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: New Year's Eve is the one night glitter is a dress code. These **40 New Year's Eve nail ideas** collect the whole countdown wardrobe: champagne gold and silver sparkle, black-and-gold drama, midnight blue glitter, confetti art and chrome party shine, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 New Year's Eve designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your midnight mood before you book. The metal sets (gold, silver and rose chrome with glitter) catch party light from across the room; the dark sets (black and gold, midnight blue, burgundy glitter) are the dramatic, photograph-all-night picks. Shapes follow the party too: stiletto and coffin carry the full glam brief, almond is the elegant middle, and short sparkle is the practical pick if you are working the night. The full collection lives in the New Year's Eve topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: NYE week is the busiest of the year, so book this set early and ask for glitter sealed under a hard gel top coat so the sparkle survives the night. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What nail colors are in for New Year's Eve 2026?
faq.a: Gold, silver and champagne glitter lead, with black-and-gold and midnight blue as the dramatic picks: design 1 (Black Gold Coffin on Dark Skin) shows the sparkle end, while design 11 (Silver Glitter Fur Cuff) shows the dark glam version wearing everywhere this season.

faq.q: Do NYE nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. Glitter concentrates beautifully at short length, and a short sparkle set is the practical party pick. Design 4 (Confetti Glitter Short Almond) and design 21 (Silver Metallic Almond Palms) prove the range keeps its shine short.

faq.q: What New Year's Eve nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Gold glitter and silver chrome are the standouts on dark and brown skin: the metal glow reads rich and the sparkle never washes out. See design 2 (Pink Glitter Almond), design 16 (Silver Glitter Short Oval) and design 31 (Neon Party Art on Dark Skin).

faq.q: How do I keep glitter nails from snagging on party clothes?
faq.a: Sealing is everything. Ask for glitter fully encapsulated under a hard gel top coat with sealed free edges, like design 26 (Black Gold Art Short Square), and the surface stays glass-smooth all night.

faq.q: When should I book my New Year's Eve set?
faq.a: Early. Countdown week books out first, so lock the appointment as soon as you pick your design; a full-glam set like design 16 (Silver Glitter Short Oval) needs the long slot.

posts.title: 25 Crazy Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Crazy nails, all 25 of them: maximalist nail art with prism galaxy chrome, dragon scales, molten gold, aquarium gel, 3D roses and python skin, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Some collections whisper. This one does not. These **25 crazy nail ideas** are the maximalist end of the NailDex catalog: prism galaxy chrome, dragon scales, molten gold dripping over black, a full aquarium inside clear gel, 3D roses, python skin and a warped checkerboard that bends the eye. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 crazy nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by nerve first, then by color. The top of the page is the wildest: galaxy chrome, flames and lightning. The middle is art-forward: koi pond, peacock feather, gothic glass. The bottom rows calm down only by comparison: opal fire, python skin and a rhinestone diamond drip. If you are booking one design for a full set, pick the one you still want to look at in two weeks; if you are mixing, take one hero design per hand and keep the rest glossy solids in the same color family.

A booking note from the tech chair: these are art appointments, not polish changes. Send your top three screenshots ahead so your tech can book the time, because designs like the aquarium and the 3D roses are built in layers. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What makes a nail design 'crazy' instead of just bold?
faq.a: Scale and layering. A bold set changes the color; a crazy set changes the texture, the dimension or the whole scene on the nail: dragon scales (design 2), a full aquarium inside clear gel (design 4) and sculpted 3D roses (design 20) all ask the nail to do something a flat polish never could.

faq.q: How long do maximalist designs like these last?
faq.a: The polish itself wears like any gel set, two to three weeks, but raised art is the weak point: 3D elements and foil can catch and lift if they are not fully encapsulated. Ask your tech to cap raised designs (like designs 3 and 20) under a builder or hard gel top so the art is sealed in, and wear gloves for cleaning.

faq.q: Which crazy design should I pick first?
faq.a: Start with the one that matches your nerve, not the loudest one on the page. Prism galaxy (design 1) is the most saved because it reads as color before it reads as art. The evil eye (design 6) is the easiest full-art pick, and opal fire (design 23) is the gateway design: wild inside, calm at a distance.

faq.q: Can these designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes, with the art scaled down: the warped checker (design 19), tiger stripes (design 12) and rainbow drip (design 22) all survive short lengths. The scene designs (aquarium, koi pond, gothic glass) need length to read properly, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below, and ask how your tech will seal raised elements. Spider web (design 13) and lightning storm (design 17) are hand-painted; crystal geode (design 8) and python skin (design 24) are texture work, and each needs its own time booked.

intro: Quiet luxury is a color palette before it is anything else: emerald, oxblood, tortoiseshell, champagne and pearls. These **25 old money nail ideas** collect the understated end of the NailDex catalog: gemstone chrome, a string of pearls down a milky nail, a gold signet on nude, herringbone tweed and marble with gold veins. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 old money nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by wardrobe first, then by finish. The deep jewel tones (emerald heirloom, ruby estate, sapphire night) carry evening and tailoring. The neutrals (cashmere beige, camel coat, mink taupe, nude silk) are the everyday-proof end of the page. The heritage details (pearl string, gold signet, equestrian chain) are the conversation pieces: one per set is plenty. If in doubt, start with tortoiseshell: it is the most booked quiet-luxury pattern in the collection.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page. Quiet luxury lives or dies on the finish, so ask for the glossiest top coat your tech carries and keep cuticle oil on daily. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are old money nails?
faq.a: Old money nails are the quiet-luxury end of nail design: rich neutrals, deep jewel tones and heritage details with an immaculate finish and no logos or noise. Think tortoiseshell (design 3), a string of pearls on milky white (design 6) and a gold signet on nude (design 9): expensive-looking because of the restraint, not the decoration.

faq.q: Which old money design should I pick first?
faq.a: Tortoiseshell (design 3) is the most booked quiet-luxury pattern and the easiest first step: it flatters every skin tone and pairs with gold jewelry. If you want a solid, emerald heirloom (design 1) is the hero of the collection; if you want the quietest possible set, nude silk (design 25) is the closer for a reason.

faq.q: Are old money nails only neutrals?
faq.a: No. The palette includes deep jewel tones: emerald, ruby estate (design 12), sapphire night (design 15) and bordeaux (design 21). What makes them old money is the finish and the restraint: one rich color, perfectly applied, rather than art on every nail.

faq.q: How do I keep quiet-luxury nails looking expensive?
faq.a: The finish is the whole look, so maintenance matters more than the design. Keep cuticle oil on daily, re-gloss with a clear top coat at the one-week mark if your tech recommends it, and never let the edges chip down: a chipped neutral reads tired faster than a chipped bright. Designs like ivory silk (design 13) and porcelain gloss (design 18) show wear first, so book fills on time.

faq.q: What nail shape suits the old money look?
faq.a: Almond and short oval are the classic choices: every design in this collection is shown on a medium almond. The heritage details (herringbone tweed, design 14; equestrian chain, design 19; marble hall, design 22) need a little length to read, while the solids work at any length, including short and natural.

intro: Chrome is not one color; it is a finish that turns every color into liquid metal. These **25 chrome nail ideas** collect the full mirror spectrum in one place: liquid silver and gold, an aurora that shifts like oil on water, holographic prism, gunmetal, black chrome and a soft moonlight pearl. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 chrome nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by metal family first, then by depth. The true metals (silver, gold, rose gold, copper, bronze, champagne) behave like jewelry and go with everything. The colored chromes (blue, purple, red, green, magenta) are the statement end. The dark mirrors (black, gunmetal, midnight, burgundy) read the most expensive after dark. If it is your first chrome set, start with silver or rose gold: they are the most forgiving and the most booked.

A booking note from the tech chair: chrome is a pigment finish rubbed over a cured base, so tell your tech you want chrome when you book, not at the chair. Bring screenshots of your top three, and ask for the top coat layering your tech prefers so the mirror stays bright. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What are chrome nails?
faq.a: Chrome nails are a mirror finish made by rubbing a fine metallic pigment over a cured gel base and sealing it under top coat. The result is liquid metal: the silver chrome (design 2) and gold chrome (design 3) in this collection are the classic versions, and every other design here is the same finish in a different color.

faq.q: How long does chrome last?
faq.a: Chrome is only as strong as its seal. Fully sandwiched under top coat, a chrome set wears like a normal gel set, around two to three weeks; under-sealed chrome rubs dull at the tips first. Ask your tech to cap the free edge carefully, especially on dark mirrors like black chrome (design 10) and midnight chrome (design 22), where wear shows fastest.

faq.q: Which chrome color should I pick first?
faq.a: Silver chrome (design 2) is the most booked because it behaves like jewelry and goes with everything. Rose gold chrome (design 4) is the warm alternative. If you want the hero, northern lights chrome (design 1) shifts pink, violet, teal and gold as your hands move, and it is the most saved design in the collection.

faq.q: Is chrome the same as metallic polish?
faq.a: No. Metallic polish has shimmer mixed through it and dries slightly textured; chrome pigment sits on the surface as a continuous mirror, which is why holographic chrome (design 17) can throw rainbow prism and pearl chrome (design 12) can glow like a shell. The mirror is the difference, and it needs the pigment step at the salon.

faq.q: Can chrome go over any base color?
faq.a: The pigment takes the color of what is under and around it, so your tech will choose a base to steer the result: dark bases deepen gunmetal (design 18) and burgundy chrome (design 20), pale bases lift ice chrome (design 24) and moonlight chrome (design 25). Show the screenshot so the base gets picked for the exact colorway you saved.

intro: The French manicure is the most booked design in nail history, and it is not one look anymore. These **25 French tip nail ideas** collect the variations worth booking in 2026: aurora chrome tips, black tips, a micro-thin petite line, a sharp V, leopard tips, a reverse French with the color at the base and a tonal nude on nude. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 French tip nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by tip first, then by base. Classic white and the petite micro line are the grow-out champions. The colored tips (red, emerald, navy, chocolate) change the whole mood without changing the structure. The special finishes (aurora, mirror, glitter, luminous pearl) are the event picks. Every design here sits on a sheer nude or pink base, which is what keeps even the neon tip looking polished.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page. A French lives on its smile line, so book a tech who hand-paints a clean line, and send the photo ahead if you want the V or the double line. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are French tip nails?
faq.a: A French manicure pairs a sheer nude or pink base with a contrasting tip, classically white (design 2). The structure never changes; the tip does. This collection collects 25 tips: aurora chrome, black, leopard, neon, a reverse French with the band at the base (design 19) and a tonal nude on nude (design 25).

faq.q: Which French design grows out best?
faq.a: The closer the tip is to a classic line, the kinder the grow-out. Classic french (design 2), petite french (design 7) with its micro-thin line and french ombre (design 14), where the white fades into the base, are the three most forgiving. Bold tips like neon french (design 23) show regrowth sooner because the contrast is higher.

faq.q: What is a reverse French?
faq.a: The mirror image of the classic: the color band sits at the base of the nail, along the cuticle, and the tip stays nude. Design 19 does it in deep red. It is a strong pick if your tips chip first, because the wear-prone end of the nail carries no color at all.

faq.q: Can French tips be done on short nails?
faq.a: Yes, and the petite french (design 7) exists for exactly that: an ultra-thin line that does not eat the nail bed visually. The V french (design 8) and double french (design 11) also suit short lengths because the geometry reads at any size. Save the wide smile lines, like cherry french (design 20), for medium and long nails.

faq.q: Which French variation should I pick first?
faq.a: If you have never worn a French, start classic (design 2) and change one variable next time: the tip color is the easiest lever, with pink french (design 5) the softest step and black french (design 3) the sharpest. Mirror french (design 17) is the event pick: a silver chrome tip that catches light like jewelry.

posts.title: 25 Jeweled Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Jeweled nails, all 25 of them: gemstone designs cut like ruby, sapphire, emerald, amethyst and diamond, with pave, cabochons and a crown jewel hero, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Every nail in this collection is a gemstone. These **25 jeweled nail ideas** are cut like the stones they are named for: a royal kaleidoscope hero, ruby marquise, sapphire cushion, emerald step cut and amethyst trillion, down to a single silver solitaire and a dusting of diamond. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 jeweled nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by stone first, then by cut. The deep stones (ruby, sapphire, garnet cabernet, onyx regalia) are the evening end. The lights (opal cabochon, moonstone mist, pearl diadem, aquamarine tide) soften the same idea for daytime. The cuts (step cut, trillion, cushion, cabochon) change how the light moves, so screenshot the exact one you want rather than describing it.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this jeweled collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are jeweled nails?
faq.a: Jeweled nails are designs built to look like cut gemstones or set jewelry: faceted color, pave crystal and cabochon stones painted or built in gel. Emerald step cut (design 4) copies a real emerald cut, and crown jewel gold (design 7) wears like a ring on the nail.

faq.q: Which jeweled design should I pick first?
faq.a: Sapphire cushion (design 3) is the most saved: a deep blue stone with a soft square cut that flatters every skin tone. Ruby marquise (design 2) is the boldest, and diamond pave (design 9) is the event pick, a full nail of tiny stones.

faq.q: Can jeweled designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like ruby Marquise (design 2) and diamond Dust (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like royal Kaleidoscope (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a jeweled set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like sapphire Cushion (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. Royal Kaleidoscope (design 1) is the hero of this collection, so if you want that exact look, send that photo when you book so the time is blocked.

posts.excerpt: Louis Vuitton nails, all 25 of them: monogram, damier checks, trunk stripes, padlocks and vachetta leather tones painted flat and flush, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: The most recognizable canvas in fashion, at nail scale. These **25 Louis Vuitton nail ideas** paint the house codes flat and flush on the nail: the monogram in brown, noir, blanc and ombre, damier checks in ebony, azur and graphite, trunk stripes, a gold padlock and vachetta leather French tips. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 Louis Vuitton nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by canvas first. The monograms (majesty, noir, bloom, eclipse, velvet, mist) are the classic end and read instantly. The damiers (ebony, azur, graphite, and the damier French) are the graphic, quieter take. The trunk details (stripes, hardware, padlock, rivet tan) are the collector details: one per set is plenty, mixed with solids in the same tan and brown family.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this louis vuitton collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are louis vuitton nails?
faq.a: Louis Vuitton nails are designer inspired designs built from the house codes: monogram canvas, damier checkerboard, trunk hardware and vachetta leather tones, all painted flat on the nail. Monogram noir (design 3) is the black version, and trunk stripes (design 5) copies the striped trunk canvas.

faq.q: Which louis vuitton design should I pick first?
faq.a: Monogram majesty (design 1) is the hero and the most saved: the full canvas with gold quatrefoil. Damier azur (design 7) is the fresh spring pick in white and blue checks, and vachetta french (design 8) is the subtle one, a leather-toned French tip.

faq.q: Can louis vuitton designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like damier Ebony (design 2) and monogram Mist (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like monogram Majesty (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a louis vuitton set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like monogram Noir (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. posts.title: 25 Rainbow Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Rainbow nails, all 25 of them: the full spectrum in marble, ombre, French tips, glitter, hologram and watercolor, from neon to pastel, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Every color, on purpose. These **25 rainbow nail ideas** collect the full spectrum in every technique: prism spectrum and spectrum swirl, rainbow marble, ombre and gradient, a prism French tip, rainbow glitter, foil, waves and a watercolor wash. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 rainbow nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by saturation first. The neon spectrum and rainbow hologram are the loud end, made for festivals and summer. The mid-page classics (marble, stripes, mosaic, clouds) read playful but polished. The pastels (pastel spectrum, pastel prism, rainbow watercolor) are the soft end that still works in an office with a dress code. One technique per set keeps the rainbow looking designed, not spilled.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this rainbow collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are rainbow nails?
faq.a: Rainbow nails use the full color spectrum in one set, either blended (ombre, marble, watercolor) or placed side by side (stripes, mosaic, hearts). Prism french (design 7) keeps the rainbow on the tips only, and spectrum drip (design 17) lets it run.

faq.q: Which rainbow design should I pick first?
faq.a: Prism spectrum (design 1) is the hero: the full spectrum with a prism shine. Rainbow ombre (design 8) is the most wearable full-color pick, and pastel spectrum (design 13) is the starter rainbow for anyone nervous about brights.

faq.q: Can rainbow designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like spectrum Swirl (design 2) and pastel Prism (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like prism Spectrum (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a rainbow set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like rainbow Marble (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. Prism Spectrum (design 1) is the hero of this collection, so if you want that exact look, send that photo when you book so the time is blocked.

posts.excerpt: Butterfly nails, all 25 of them: butterflies in chrome, morpho blue, monarch orange, aura, glitter and marble, plus butterfly French tips and pearls, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: One motif, twenty-five species of pretty. These **25 butterfly nail ideas** paint the butterfly every way it can be painted: monarch chrome and blue morpho, a butterfly garden, pink and violet butterflies, a butterfly French tip, gold butterflies, an aura wash and a black butterfly for contrast. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 butterfly nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by species color first. The monarch family (chrome, tips, sunset) is orange and graphic. The morpho and teal butterflies are the blue end. The pastels (pastel butterfly, baby butterfly, whisper butterfly) are the soft end that suits spring and shorter nails. Placement matters too: a full-wing design wants length, while butterfly pearls and the French version read at any size.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this butterfly collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are butterfly nails?
faq.a: Butterfly nails feature butterfly wings or whole butterflies as the art, in finishes from chrome to glitter to marble. Butterfly aura (design 8) fades the wings into an aura gradient, and butterfly velvet (design 21) gives them a matte velvet finish.

faq.q: Which butterfly design should I pick first?
faq.a: Monarch chrome (design 1) is the hero, orange wings with a chrome shine. Butterfly french (design 6) is the subtle pick, wings on the tips only, and blue morpho (design 2) is the most photographed color on the page.

faq.q: Can butterfly designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like blue Morpho (design 2) and whisper Butterfly (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like monarch Chrome (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a butterfly set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like butterfly Garden (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

posts.excerpt: Old money red nails, all 25 of them: quiet-luxury reds in garnet, claret, oxblood and bordeaux with tortoise, pearl, cameo and gold filigree details, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Old money style has a red chapter, and it is not bright red. These **25 old money red nail ideas** work the deep, inherited end of red: garnet chrome and heritage red, claret silk, an oxblood French, rouge tortoise, pearl rouge and cherrywood, with cameos, estate seals and gold filigree. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 old money red nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by depth first. The garnets and claret (garnet chrome, heritage red, claret silk, antique ruby) are the richest and read like jewelry. The browns of red (cherrywood, rosewood, library leather, rouge tortoise) are the heritage end that pairs with tweed and gold. The details (estate seal, cameo rouge, pinstripe red, heirloom stripe, gold filigree) are one-nail statements over a matching solid.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this old money red collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are old money red nails?
faq.a: Old money red nails are quiet-luxury designs in deep, muted reds, garnet, claret, oxblood, bordeaux, with heritage details and an immaculate finish. Rouge noir (design 12) is nearly black red, and bordeaux ombre (design 24) fades the depth out.

faq.q: Which old money red design should I pick first?
faq.a: Garnet chrome (design 1) is the hero, a deep red with a chrome glow. Heritage red (design 2) is the most booked solid, and oxblood french (design 4) is the quiet-luxury French, deep red on the tips only.

faq.q: Can old money red designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like heritage Red (design 2) and rouge Veil (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like garnet Chrome (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a old money red set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like claret Silk (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?

posts.title: 25 Black Halloween Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Black Halloween nails, all 25 of them: every design on a black base, onyx eclipse, gilded jack, skull cameo, widow web, chrome bones and a void matte closer, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Every design in this collection starts from black, and black does all the haunting. These **25 black Halloween nail ideas** run from an onyx eclipse hero through a gilded jack, skull cameo, widow web and bat cave to chrome bones, a serpent coil and a thorn rose, ending in pure void matte. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 black Halloween nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by contrast first. The gold on black designs (gilded jack, skull cameo, manor lights, candle vigil, bone moon) are the elegant end, black tie Halloween. The creatures (bat cave, raven perch, serpent coil, scorpion sting, moth nocturne) are silhouette work. The red accents (scarlet fangs, blood ink, thorn rose) are the only color allowed, and they earn it.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this black halloween collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are black halloween nails?
faq.a: Black Halloween nails keep every design on a black base and let gold, silver, bone white or a single red accent do the art. Apothecary glow (design 10) lights one green candle of color, and planchette (design 21) is the ouija detail pick.

faq.q: Which black halloween design should I pick first?
faq.a: Onyx eclipse (design 1) is the hero, black on black with a single eclipse of light. Widow web (design 4) is the most saved, and void matte (design 25) is the closer: pure matte black, the scariest plain nail on the page.

faq.q: Can black halloween designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like gilded Jack (design 2) and void Matte (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like onyx Eclipse (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a black halloween set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like skull Cameo (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. Onyx Eclipse (design 1) is the hero of this collection, so if you want that exact look, send that photo when you book so the time is blocked.

posts.excerpt: Candy nails, all 25 of them: the candy shop as nail art, Skittles, gummy bears, lollipop swirls, peppermint, jelly beans, rock candy and a ring pop finale, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: The candy shop, worn on your hands. These **25 candy nail ideas** turn the classics into nail art: a Skittles hero and M&M's, gummy bears, a lollipop swirl, peppermint cane, jelly beans, rock candy, sour worms and a Hershey kiss, ending with a ring pop. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 candy nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by candy first, obviously. The rainbow candies (Skittles, jelly beans, candy kernels, nerds, candy buttons) are the color explosion end. The swirls (lollipop swirl, peppermint pinwheel, marshmallow twist, bubble gum) are pattern and movement. The chocolate corner (Hershey kiss, chocolate truffles, toffee crunch) is the warm, wearable end of the shop.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this candy collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are candy nails?
faq.a: Candy nails copy real candy, colors, shapes and shine, in gel: glossy like a jawbreaker (design 14), twisted like licorice wheels (design 16), or soft like a cotton candy cloud (design 10).

faq.q: Which candy design should I pick first?
faq.a: Skittles (design 1) is the hero, the whole rainbow in candy form. Gummy bears (design 3) is the most saved, and peppermint cane (design 5) is the holiday crossover that books from November on.

faq.q: Can candy designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like m&M'S (design 2) and ring Pop (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like skittles (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a candy set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like gummy Bears (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

intro: Nail art from about twenty years in the future. These **25 futuristic nail ideas** run on chrome, plasma and holograms: a neural chrome hero, plasma rose, quantum glass, cyber onyx, an aurora coil, a laser lattice and mercury bloom, through glitch prisms and titanium lace to an android bloom. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 futuristic nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by technology first. The chromes (neural chrome, chrome eclipse, mercury bloom, titanium lace) are liquid metal and read like hardware. The energy designs (plasma rose, acid reactor, ultraviolet wave, hyperdrive, photon circuit) glow in acid and neon. The bio-tech end (alien orchid, holo butterfly, spectral serpent, android bloom, liquid opal) grows the future instead of building it.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this futuristic collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are futuristic nails?
faq.a: Futuristic nails use sci-fi materials and patterns, chrome, hologram, glass, circuits and plasma color, to make nails look engineered rather than painted. Crystal matrix (design 13) grows geometry, and nanofiber silk (design 17) weaves it.

faq.q: Which futuristic design should I pick first?
faq.a: Neural chrome (design 1) is the hero, circuit patterns in liquid chrome. Quantum glass (design 3) is the most saved, transparent and strange, and holo butterfly (design 9) is the soft entry into the future.

faq.q: Can futuristic designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like plasma Rose (design 2) and android Bloom (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like neural Chrome (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a futuristic set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like quantum Glass (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. Neural Chrome (design 1) is the hero of this collection, so if you want that exact look, send that photo when you book so the time is blocked.

posts.title: 25 Fairytale Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Fairytale nails, all 25 of them: storybook nail art with a glass slipper, enchanted rose, poisoned apple, pumpkin carriage, magic wand and a storybook castle, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Once upon a time, on a fingernail. These **25 fairytale nail ideas** paint the storybook shelf: a glass slipper hero, an enchanted rose, a poisoned apple, a pumpkin carriage, a magic wand and a spinning wheel, through a gingerbread cottage and Red Riding Hood to a storybook castle. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 fairytale nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by story first. The princess pieces (glass slipper, enchanted rose, pumpkin carriage, golden egg, rapunzel braid, swan feather) are the romantic end in pink, gold and pearl. The woodland tales (gingerbread cottage, red riding hood, three bears, frog prince, puss in boots) are warmer and more playful. The magic objects (magic wand, magic mirror, wishing well, golden key, pixie dust) work one per set as an accent story.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this fairytale collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are fairytale nails?
faq.a: Fairytale nails illustrate classic stories, the objects and moments everyone knows: the slipper, the rose under glass, the apple. Snow queen (design 20) is the icy chapter, and gem mine (design 15) is the dwarfs' workplace.

faq.q: Which fairytale design should I pick first?
faq.a: Glass slipper (design 1) is the hero, transparent and sparkling. Enchanted rose (design 2) is the most saved, and poisoned apple (design 3) is the villain twist everyone screenshots at Halloween.

faq.q: Can fairytale designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like enchanted Rose (design 2) and storybook Castle (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like glass Slipper (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a fairytale set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like poisoned Apple (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. Glass Slipper (design 1) is the hero of this collection, so if you want that exact look, send that photo when you book so the time is blocked.

posts.excerpt: Fruit nails, all 25 of them: fruit as nail art, a strawberry jewel, watermelon slice, pineapple crown, kiwi, cherries, citrus and a dragon fruit finale, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: The fruit bowl, but make it nail art. These **25 fruit nail ideas** slice the orchard onto nails: a strawberry jewel hero, a watermelon slice, a pineapple crown, a kiwi half, a cherry pair and a lemon slice, through grapes, peaches and pomegranate to a dragon fruit finale. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 fruit nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by fruit first. The reds (strawberry jewel, cherry pair, raspberry gem, pomegranate jewel, watermelon slice) are the juicy classics. The citrus (lemon slice, lime wedge, orange slice, mandarin segment) is the bright, zesty end. The exotics (passion fruit, dragon fruit, star fruit, fig half, coconut half) are the conversation pieces, detailed and tropical.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this fruit collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are fruit nails?
faq.a: Fruit nails paint fruit, whole, sliced and jeweled, in true fruit colors with a juicy gloss. Mango cheek (design 10) and peach bloom (design 8) are the soft stone fruit end, and grape cluster (design 7) is the vineyard pick.

faq.q: Which fruit design should I pick first?
faq.a: Strawberry jewel (design 1) is the hero, a strawberry cut like a gem. Watermelon slice (design 2) is the summer classic everyone saves, and cherry pair (design 5) is the cute, simple pick that works on short nails.

faq.q: Can fruit designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like watermelon Slice (design 2) and dragon Fruit (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like strawberry Jewel (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a fruit set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like pineapple Crown (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

intro: A whole garden, alive on your nails. These **25 garden nail ideas** collect the living garden: a garden butterfly hero, a peony gem, a hummingbird gem, a dragonfly jewel, a ladybird dot and honey bee gold, through ivy vine pearl and dew drop crystal to a butterfly crown. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 garden nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by inhabitant first. The creatures (butterfly, hummingbird, dragonfly, ladybird, honey bee, firefly glow) move the garden across the set. The flowers (peony, dahlia, tulip, lavender, sunflower, orchid, poppy, lotus, wisteria, camellia) are the bloom end, one flower family per set reads most designed. The details (ivy vine pearl, dew drop crystal, daisy chain pearl, fern frond gold, garden gate gold) finish a set like edging finishes a bed.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this garden collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

posts.title: 25 Soft Gel Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Soft gel nails, all 25 of them: translucent jelly and syrup gels, milky glass nails and sheer layered color in cherry, raspberry, sky, mint and nude syrup, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Soft gel is a texture before it is a color: translucent, syrupy, light passing through. These **25 soft gel nail ideas** collect the jelly and glass family: a cherry syrup hero, sapphire jelly, coral syrup, raspberry glass, teal glass and plum syrup, through mint, sky and grape to a cloud jelly closer. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 soft gel nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by flavor first, because these are named like syrups for a reason. The reds and berries (cherry syrup, raspberry glass, berry glass, rose syrup, fuchsia syrup) are the juicy end. The blues and greens (sapphire jelly, teal glass, sky glass, mint glass, pistachio jelly) are the cool glass end. The neutrals (nude syrup, pearl glass, cloud jelly, baby pink jelly) are the clean, milky everyday versions.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this soft gel collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are soft gel nails?
faq.a: Soft gel nails use translucent jelly and syrup gel polishes that let light through, layered for depth, with a dewy high gloss. Amber syrup (design 13) is the warm honey version, and mahogany glass (design 20) is the deep, grown-up one.

faq.q: Which soft gel design should I pick first?
faq.a: Cherry syrup (design 1) is the hero, the juiciest red in glass form. Raspberry glass (design 4) is the most saved, and nude syrup (design 19) is the clean girl version that goes with everything.

faq.q: Can soft gel designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like sapphire Jelly (design 2) and cloud Jelly (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like cherry Syrup (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a soft gel set last?
faq.a: Like any gel set, two to three weeks with normal care. The finish is the weak point on detailed work: ask your tech to fully seal designs like coral Syrup (design 3) under a strong top coat, cap the free edge, and keep cuticle oil on daily so the shine survives to your fill.

faq.q: What should I ask my nail tech for?
faq.a: Bring the screenshot and book it as an art set, not a polish change. Say the design name, the base color and the finish from the design card below. Cherry Syrup (design 1) is the hero of this collection, so if you want that exact look, send that photo when you book so the time is blocked.

posts.title: 25 Simple Holiday Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Simple holiday nails, all 25 of them: clean solids in holiday colors, tiny single accents, simple French tips with festive edges and fine glitter gradients, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Simple is a discipline, not a shortcut. These **25 simple holiday nail ideas** keep every design to one idea: a glossy solid in a holiday color, a single tiny snowflake, one holly sprig on a French tip, a hairline of gold at the edge. The crimson magnet hero proves a solid can still have depth. Every photo below is drawn from the 25 simple holiday nail designs in the NailDex catalog collection.

Pick by effort first. The solids (deep pine gloss, winter cranberry, cocoa gloss, burgundy gloss) are one-color appointments that still read holiday. The French tips (holly french, scarlet french, pine french, gold edge french, gold line french) keep the base sheer and put the season at the edge. The gradients and veils (berry gradient, frost veil, gilded gradient) are the soft middle.

A booking note from the tech chair: bring screenshots of your top three from this page and send them ahead when you book, because the detailed designs in this simple holiday collection need art time, not a polish change slot. Each design below includes the exact words to ask for, including the finish, so what you leave with matches what you saved.

faq.q: What are simple holiday nails?
faq.a: Simple holiday nails are Christmas-season designs reduced to one clean idea per nail: a solid holiday color, a single small motif, or a classic French tip with a festive edge. Crimson magnet (design 1) and holly french (design 6) are the two poles of the collection.

faq.q: Which simple holiday design should I pick first?
faq.a: Crimson magnet (design 1) is the hero: a deep red cat-eye with a glowing band, simple in shape and rich in finish. Lone snowflake (design 7) is the signature simple pick, one snowflake on ice blue, and snowfall gloss (design 25) is the quiet closer.

faq.q: Can simple holiday designs be done on short nails?
faq.a: Most of them, yes. The single-motif and simpler designs, like deep Pine Gloss (design 2) and snowfall Gloss (design 25), scale down cleanly to short lengths. The detailed scene and placement designs, like crimson Magnet (design 1), need more canvas, so grow or extend first if your heart is set on those.

faq.q: How long does a simple holiday set last?

The greens (emerald jewel gloss, holly green gloss, evergreen pine gloss, forest velvet) pair with gold. The metals (champagne gold chrome, icy silver chrome, copper garland metal, silver tinsel chrome) are the party finishes, and the pearls (frost white pearl, spiced cream pearl, ivory pearl glow) are the quiet end.
